headline: Recommended approval, as amended, of zoning changes for protected accessory dwelling units to align with state law.
summary: The amended proposal would cap backyard cottages at 1.5 stories and 1,152 total square feet of gross floor area. Public comments on the zoning proposal are accepted until October 30, 2026. The committee also recommended withdrawing a separate zoning amendment by Councilor Link and approved minutes from two earlier meetings.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 1, 2026 Land Use Committee meeting, 5-0.
Approved the minutes of the October 15, 2026 Land Use Committee meeting, 5-0.
Approved replacing the text of item 26-1336 with the PADU compliance amendment, 5-0.
Recommended approval, as amended, of the zoning amendment on protected accessory dwelling units, 5-0.
Recommended withdrawing the zoning amendment to Section 3.1.7.c proposed by Councilor Link, 5-0.

## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Land Use Committee Meeting Minutes

Thursday, October 29, 2026

6:30 PM

This meeting was held via Zoom and was called to order by Chair Ewen-Campen at 6:34 pm and adjourned at 7:45pm on a roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilors Davis, Clingan, Sait, McLaughlin, Ewen-Campen), 0 opposed, and 0 absent.

Others present: Dan Bartman – Director of Planning and Zoning, Samantha Carr – Land Use Analyst, Madalyn Letellier – Assistant City Clerk, Legislative Services.

- Present: Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis, Ward Four City

3. Mayor's Request Requesting ordainment of an amendment to Sections 3.1.3, 3.1.6, 3.1.8, (ID # 26-1336 ) 3.1.9, 3.1.11, 3.1.12, 3.1.13, 3.1.16, 3.2.6 of the Somerville Zoning

- Ordinance to align with State Law regarding protected accessory dwelling
- units.

- Chair Ewen-Campen shared that the administration’s ground-floor dwelling

proposal was amended to incorporate Councilor Link's amendments. It was amended to better align with state law, the body reviewed a proposal

capping backyard cottages at 1.5 stories and 1,152 total square feet of gross floor area. Land Use Analyst Samantha Carr clarified that gross floor area

includes lofts and floor tiers. In response to Councilor Clingan Analyst Carr and Director Bartman confirmed that basements, whether they are finished

or unfinished, are excluded from total gross floor area. Basements only count as a full story if the finished floor sits at least 5 feet above ground level and would allow a half story of livable space as state regulations would count the basement as the first story.

In discussion and in response to questions from Councilors it was noted that for enforcement and compliance, unpermitted, non-compliant livable spaces

- are difficult to identify unless explicitly reported by a constituent. Director

- Bartman stated that the Inspectional Services Department (ISD) handles

permitting incentives, and the legal department will review whether the state must regulate these specific accessory dwelling unit (ADU) interpretations

or if the local regulations can remain more permissive. Director Bartman also noted that while the state allows two stories over a garage, this local amendment restricts the total allowable stories. Finally, instead of adding back floor plate maximums, the regulations will rely on total gross floor

- area, which allows for flexible, non-stacked layouts.

Chair Ewen-Campen moved to replace the text in item #26-1336 with the language in the attachment Land Use - 2026-10-29 PADU

Compliance Amendment (with 26-1336) . The motion was approved on a

roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilor Davis, Clingan, Sait, McLaughlin, Ewen-Campen), 0 opposed.

- Chair Ewen-Campen clarified no decisions would be made on the item until
- the public hearing comment period was closed. Comments are accepted until

October 30, 2026, to be submitted as part of the public hearing and comments are always accepted to the City Council at

- publiccomments@somervillema.gov.

AMENDED
